To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the higher the unemployment rate, the higher the NPLs the higher the ROE, the lower the NPLs and the higher the economic growth, the lower the non performing loans.
the unemployment rate, GDP, BRMR and EAPV are statistically significant and relevant for the NPLs of the Romanian Banking Systems.
the NPLs are positively influenced by the unemployment rate, negatively influenced by the GDP growth and ROE, and are also positively influenced by LTD and BRMR.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the determinants of non performing loans, for the largest five Romanian banks.
the identification of the determinants of Non performing loans in the Romanian Banking System.
the impact of macroeconomic indicators and bank specific variables on NPLs in Romania.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the BRMR variable has a negative impact, while EAPV is positive correlated with NLPs.
the NPLs are positively correlated with unemployment rate and negatively with ROE, GDP growth rate and BRMR.
the qualitative variables introduced in the model have the same impact as the quantitative ones, the results being statistically significant.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the BRMR variable has the highest impact on NPL, being negative correlated with such loans and that the EAPV variable has the lowest impact, being positive correlated with such loans.
the qualitative variables have a significant impact on the NPLs and that they should be considered as important factors when analyzing the credit risk of the banking sector.

the NPLs are influenced by a series of variables and the decision making process should take in consideration the qualitative ones as well, for an efficient and sustainable management of the banking sector.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the BRMR is positively correlated with NPL ratio and EAPV is negatively correlated with NPL.
the introduction of these qualitative variables in the regression model, along with the quantitative ones, provides a more accurate model for NPLs decision making.
the qualitative variables are relevant for explaining the NPLs, the BRMR variable having an impact on NPL ratio and EAPV being relevant for the ROE.
